clue.text: Lament plot about a heartless Australian crook?

indicators.note: about means turned round, so the word for plot is read from its end back to its start
without a heart, the word loses its central letter

blocks.note: a web of intrigue is a plot
taken as written
in Australian slang, crook means sick

explanation.surface: Someone bemoans a scheme involving a dodgy Australian villain.
explanation.walkthrough: In Australian slang, feeling crook means feeling unwell; the question mark flags this sense, as the surface wants a criminal.
explanation.definitionFit: To bewail something is to express great sorrow over it, a close synonym of lament.

clue.text: Part of formal debate raised uproar

indicators.note: part of tells us the letters sit inside the following words
in a down clue, raised means the letters read upwards, from bottom to top

blocks.note: the letters spanning the end of formal and the start of debate

explanation.surface: A section of a formal debate turned into chaos.
explanation.definitionFit: Bedlam, named after a notorious London asylum, means a scene of noisy confusion or uproar.

clue.text: Discovered outstanding detective shed tears, being exposed

indicators.note: dis-covered means stripped of its cover, so the outer letters are taken away

blocks.note: money outstanding is still owing
DS stands for Detective Sergeant
to weep is to shed tears

explanation.surface: An outstanding detective, found out, broke down in tears and felt exposed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Discovered' reads as found out, but it means uncover: OWING loses its first and last letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A windswept place lies open to strong winds, which is what being exposed means here; the adjective phrase fits.

clue.text: Vast space store vacated, one two miles to the north

indicators.note: something vacated is emptied, so only the outer letters of the word stay
in a down clue, north is the top, so these pieces are written above the others

blocks.note: Roman numeral one
M is the abbreviation for mile, twice
an en is a printer's space
taken as written

explanation.surface: A huge storage space has been emptied, with one or two miles to the north.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue, 'to the north' puts I and MM above the rest; STORE vacated leaves just S and E.
explanation.definitionFit: Immense means extremely large in size, a direct synonym of vast.

clue.text: Almost nobody is attracted to violent film

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the last letter is dropped

blocks.note: violent winds or seas are called high
nobody is no one

explanation.surface: Hardly anyone is drawn to films full of violence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Is attracted to' means the shortened NO ONE attaches itself after HIGH.
explanation.definitionFit: High Noon is the 1952 western starring Gary Cooper, so it is an example of a film.

clue.text: Evil career developed smuggling gin, ultimately something unimportant

indicators.note: something developed has changed form, so these letters are reworked
ultimately points to the final letter of the following word

blocks.note: the anagram fodder
the last letter of gin

explanation.surface: A wicked career built up by smuggling gin, which in the end proved trivial.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Smuggling' tells us the N is taken into the mix of EVIL CAREER before it is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: An irrelevance is a thing of no importance or bearing on the matter, a noun matching 'something unimportant'.

clue.text: Modern jazz fan in short trousers

indicators.note: short means cut off, so the word loses its final letter

blocks.note: hipsters are low-waisted trousers

explanation.surface: A fan of modern jazz is wearing short trousers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Short trousers' looks like a garment, but short is the instruction to clip HIPSTERS.
explanation.definitionFit: The original 1940s hipsters were devotees of bebop, the modern jazz of that time.

clue.text: Whatever they recorded from disc remaining unaltered

blocks.note: O is round like a disc
something left as is remains unaltered

explanation.surface: Whatever they put on record came off the disc unchanged.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Whatever' is a 1994 single by the band, so 'Whatever they recorded' points to the group who recorded it.
explanation.definitionFit: Oasis, the Manchester rock band, released the hit single Whatever, so they are the ones who recorded it.

clue.text: Name 9 swimming across river somewhere in France

indicators.note: swimming letters move about freely, so they are rearranged
across means stretched over, so the letters enclose the next item

blocks.note: N is the abbreviation for name
the answer to 9 Across
R is the abbreviation for river

explanation.surface: An energetic person swims across a river somewhere in France.
explanation.walkthrough: The R goes inside the rearranged DYNAMO, then N goes in front.
explanation.definitionFit: Normandy is a region of northern France, so it is a place in that country.

clue.text: Around so many devotees welcoming energetic individual

indicators.note: around means turned back, so the letters are read right to left
the words welcome the answer, holding it inside them

blocks.note: the letters run from the end of so to the start of devotees

explanation.surface: A lively person is surrounded by a crowd of devoted fans.
explanation.definitionFit: A dynamo, literally a generator, is figuratively a person bursting with energy and drive.

clue.text: Expert model, one going down on bended knee?

definitions.text: one going down on bended knee?

blocks.note: a pro is an expert
a model poses for artists

explanation.surface: A professional model kneels, as if about to pop the question.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags a definition by example: kneeling is how a marriage proposal is traditionally made.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone proposing marriage traditionally kneels on one knee, so the proposer is the person going down.

clue.text: Vince regularly enters club containing very noxious element

indicators.note: regularly means at even intervals, so every other letter is kept
enters means goes inside, so these letters sit within the next word

blocks.note: Arsenal is a London football club
the second and fourth letters

explanation.surface: Vince often turns up at a club that has something poisonous about it.
explanation.walkthrough: Arsenal is a London football club; IC goes in after its fifth letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Arsenical describes something containing arsenic, the notoriously poisonous element.

clue.text: Payment method succeeded for any number accessing item from Specsavers?

indicators.note: for here means in place of, so one letter swaps in where another stood

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for succeeded
N is the algebraic symbol for an unspecified number
Specsavers is a high-street optician chain

explanation.surface: Paying for something at an optician with a card tap.
explanation.walkthrough: Specsavers is a British chain of opticians. In CONTACT LENS, S takes the place of N, the letter 'accessing' the item.
explanation.definitionFit: Contactless payment means tapping a card or phone on a reader, a method of paying for goods.

clue.text: Abuse when cycling for inventor

indicators.note: cycling means rotating, so letters move from the front of the word round to the back

blocks.note: to slate is to criticise harshly

explanation.surface: Someone is insulted while out on a bike, in a jibe aimed at an inventor.
explanation.walkthrough: Move SL from the front of SLATE to the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Nikola Tesla was the Serbian-American inventor behind alternating current systems.

clue.text: Hire-purchase scheme deposit in place that's perfect

blocks.note: British slang for buying on credit by instalments
to land is to set down or deposit

explanation.surface: Putting down a deposit on a hire-purchase deal for an ideal home.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain, buying on the never-never means paying by hire purchase.
explanation.definitionFit: Never Never Land is Peter Pan's island, and by extension any imaginary ideal place.

clue.text: PM abroad often or visiting land's interior?

indicators.note: abroad means scattered widely, so these letters are spread and rearranged
the interior is the inside, so only the middle letters are kept

blocks.note: the anagram fodder
the inner letters of land

explanation.surface: A prime minister often goes overseas or travels inland.
explanation.walkthrough: PM looks like Prime Minister but is post meridiem. 'Visiting' takes AN into the jumbled letters.
explanation.definitionFit: PM, from Latin post meridiem, marks the hours after midday, the afternoon.

clue.text: Supporter of tennis player formerly adopting coach's tips

indicators.note: tips are the ends, so the first and last letters of the word are kept
adopting means taking in, so the letters are placed inside

blocks.note: Tim Henman, a British tennis player now retired
first and last letters of coach

explanation.surface: A retired tennis star's backer takes on board the coach's advice.
explanation.walkthrough: Tim Henman was Britain's leading men's tennis player around 2000; 'tips' looks like advice but means ends.
explanation.definitionFit: A henchman is a loyal follower or right-hand man, a backer of a leader.

clue.text: Intense natter about embracing male pastimes

indicators.note: about means all around, so these letters are turned about into a new order
embracing means holding within, so a letter goes inside

blocks.note: the anagram fodder
M is the abbreviation for male

explanation.surface: An earnest chat about men's hobbies.
explanation.definitionFit: Entertainments are amusements that pass the time, so they are hobbies or pastimes by another name.

clue.text: Managed Palace, with no time for acrimony

indicators.note: with no time means the letter abbreviating time is removed

blocks.note: to run a business is to manage it
a royal palace is a court

explanation.surface: Someone ran a palace but lacked time for bitterness.
explanation.walkthrough: T, the symbol for time, drops out of COURT.
explanation.definitionFit: Rancour is deep-seated bitterness or resentment, which is what acrimony means.

clue.text: Ascetic purchases Charlie perfume

indicators.note: purchases means takes hold of, so one piece is held inside another

blocks.note: the Essenes were an ascetic Jewish sect
Charlie is C in the NATO alphabet

explanation.surface: A self-denying person splashes out on a bottle of Charlie scent.
explanation.walkthrough: Charlie was a popular Revlon perfume, which makes 'Charlie perfume' read as a product.
explanation.definitionFit: Essence is a concentrated extract used as a scent, so it can stand for perfume.

clue.text: Cool releases on the radio

indicators.note: on the radio means heard rather than read, so the sound counts

blocks.note: to free is to release

explanation.surface: Laid-back new tracks being played over the airwaves.
explanation.definitionFit: To freeze is to make very cold, a verb that can stand in for cool.

clue.text: Conservative minister interrupted by Posh Spice

indicators.note: interrupted by means broken into, so a letter is placed within

blocks.note: C is the abbreviation for Conservative
MIN is the abbreviation for minister
U means upper-class

explanation.surface: A Tory minister is heckled by Posh Spice of the Spice Girls.
explanation.walkthrough: Posh Spice (Victoria Beckham) seems to be a single name, but Spice is the definition and Posh gives U.
explanation.definitionFit: Cumin is the aromatic seed widely used as a spice in curries.

clue.text: Worth being married prior to tax going up?

indicators.note: in a down clue, going up means the letters are read from bottom to top
prior to means coming before, fixing the order of the pieces

blocks.note: M is the abbreviation for married
to tax someone is to tire them

explanation.surface: Is it worth getting married before the tax bill rises?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Prior to' places M before the rest; tax is a verb meaning to strain, not a levy.
explanation.definitionFit: Merit is a quality deserving praise, so it is a synonym of worth.

clue.text: Star heard occasionally ringing American firm for fund manager

indicators.note: occasionally means now and then, so only every other letter is used
ringing means encircling, so these letters surround what follows

blocks.note: the even letters of the two words
A is the abbreviation for American
firm and sure both mean steady and certain

explanation.surface: A celebrity is said to be ringing a US company to get someone to look after the money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heard' looks like a homophone signal but is only part of the letter source for the alternate letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A treasurer is the officer in charge of an organisation's funds, so it is a manager of funds.

clue.text: Tabloid journalist reflected

blocks.note: the Mirror is a British tabloid newspaper
ED is short for editor

explanation.surface: A tabloid reporter thought things over.
explanation.walkthrough: The Daily Mirror is a British tabloid. 'Reflected' tempts as pondered, but it means shown as in a glass.
explanation.definitionFit: Mirrored means reproduced as in a looking glass, so it means reflected as an image.

clue.text: Poles needing nap in Glasgow nod off

blocks.note: south and north are the two poles
ooze or oose is Scots for fluff, the nap of cloth

explanation.surface: Polish people need a nap in Glasgow so they can drift off.
explanation.walkthrough: Nap here is the raised fibre on cloth, not a doze; Glasgow signals the Scots word for fluff.
explanation.definitionFit: To snooze is to have a light sleep, so it means the same as to nod off.

clue.text: Mistakenly start uni as someone who'll reveal all?

indicators.note: something done mistakenly comes out wrong, so the letters land in the wrong order

blocks.note: the anagram fodder

explanation.surface: A student starts university by mistake as someone who'll tell all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reveal all' suggests telling secrets; the question mark flags the joke that it means baring the body.
explanation.definitionFit: A naturist goes without clothes, so in a literal sense they bare everything.

clue.text: Hat that is placed on head

indicators.note: placed on means put after in an across clue, as the first item rests upon the second

blocks.note: bean is slang for head
i.e. is the abbreviation for that is

explanation.surface: A hat, that is, something placed on the head.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as a plain description of a hat, hiding that 'head' is slang to be put underneath the abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: A beanie is a close-fitting knitted hat, so it is one kind of hat.
